**Issue #3014 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3014: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 41797690342](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41797690342) on `main` (`004c2ae`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [e2e (7/8)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41797690342/job/126471646172) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `main`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`): production promotes itself only from a run on `main` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41802830121)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Fix the red `e2e (7/8)` job from super run 41797690342 (on `main` at `004c2ae`, workflow_dispatch) so the next daily run passes every job and production can promote. Name the failed job in the pull request and how it was checked. Never skip, disable, or quarantine a test, and never raise a timeout.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/cypress/e2e/13-practice-vs-ai.cy.ts` | change (prime suspect) | Hard/Medium expectation that #3006's mulligan change broke (opening-hand, first-turn, or replay-hash fold assertions) |
| `e2e/cypress/e2e/10-invite-gate.cy.ts` | change only if it is the failing spec | Flaky invite/reseed assertion made robust |
| `e2e/cypress/e2e/15-audio.cy.ts`, `17-card-showcase-and-hovers.cy.ts`, `25-overflow-animations.cy.ts`, `31-counter-opponent-turn.cy.ts`, `38-accessibility.cy.ts`, `48-tutorial-final-exam.cy.ts` | change only the one that fails | The failing assertion made deterministic (retried assertions, seed documented below) |
| `e2e/support/practice.ts` | change only if root cause is in `keepWholeHand`, `reachHumanTurn`, or `settledThroughAiTurn` | Helper fix, same behavior contract |
| `e2e/support/chrome-pin.ts` | change only if failure is the Chrome-155 socket drop with the pin not engaging | `BROKEN_CHROME_MAJORS` / `PINNED_CHROME_MILESTONE` handling |
| `apps/web/src/<owning module>` | change only if a product bug (not a test bug) is found | The one component/layer that owns the bug, no unrelated edits |

Do not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`; `crates/ai/src/mulligan.rs` and `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (#3006's behavior is intended and ruled); `spec/rulings/R2977000.md`; any timeout value. Governing spec: R2977000 (AI mulligan bound), R144 (server reseed), R181/R180 (handicaps), R187 (replay hash).

## Steps

1. Compute shard 7's spec list and confirm it matches the failing run: run `node e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs 7 8` from `e2e/`. It must print `10-invite-gate, 13-practice-vs-ai, 15-audio, 17-card-showcase-and-hovers, 25-overflow-animations, 31-counter-opponent-turn, 38-accessibility, 48-tutorial-final-exam`. (`shard-specs.mjs` and these specs are unchanged since `004c2ae`, so the list is the run's list.)
2. Reproduce with the job's own path, locally: `pnpm --dir apps/web build:e2e`; serve it with `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vite preview --port 5173 --strictPort`; boot a release server with `E2E=1 cargo run --release -p jackioh-server` (fresh boot per attempt, per R144; spec 10 reseeds itself). Then from `e2e/`: `E2E_ARTIFACTS=artifacts/issue-3014 pnpm exec cypress run --browser chrome --spec <the shard-7 list>`. Use `E2E_CHROME_PIN=1` if system Chrome is major 155.
3. Read the failure output and name the single failing spec and test. Inspect that test's assertions first, in this order: (a) in spec 13, the Hard game's first-turn observability (`HARD_SEED`, `keepWholeHand`, `opponentMax` data-max=2 block) and the `replayHash` folds — #3006 changed exactly the AI's kept opening hand for mana-bonus seats; (b) in specs 10/38, `Couldn't reach JackiOh` or dropped-socket errors (Chrome-155 flake, see `e2e/README.md`); (c) in 15/25/48, animation/coach-timing assertions (`MOVE_BUDGET`, recorder samples).
4. Root-cause before editing: rerun only the failing spec against a second fresh server boot. A failure that moves between tests or passes on reboot is the Chrome socket flake or a timing flake, not AI behavior — fix the test's robustness, not the product. A failure that repeats on the same assertion with the same seed is deterministic — the assertion disagrees with intended behavior since #3006.
5. Apply the smallest robust fix: prefer a retried Cypress assertion (`should` on an already-exposed testid) over new waits; add no `cy.wait(ms)` (spec 13's header bans it) and raise no timeout. If the assertion encodes pre-#3006 AI behavior (e.g., a Hard opening hand that must now keep a 4-drop per R2977000), update the expectation to the ruled behavior and cite R2977000 in a comment. If a seed no longer yields its documented setup (e.g., `HARD_SEED` "yields an observable first AI turn"), pick the nearest seed that does and update the comment saying what the seed yields.
6. If the root cause is a product bug in `apps/web/src` (visible wrong behavior, not just test timing), fix it in its owning module only, following the code around it, with named constants per rule 9.
7. Re-run the full shard-7 list from step 2 to green on a fresh server boot. Then run the checks in Tests.

## Tests

- `node e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs 7 8` (shard list matches the failed job).
- Full shard-7 Cypress run on Chrome per step 2, green on a fresh boot; on failure, the run's screenshots under `artifacts/issue-3014` are the evidence.
- For any touched e2e helper or web unit file: `pnpm --dir apps/web test <that test file>` (builds the WASM module first).
- `cargo fmt --check`; if a Rust file was touched, `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p <crate> <test name>`.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` only if a ruling note or `proven_in` was touched (not expected).
- The pull request text names job `e2e (7/8)` of the super run and says the fix was checked by the local shard-7 reproduction above (a pull request's CI runs only e2e smoke specs, so the daily shard is checked locally, not on the pull request).

## Done when

- [ ] The failing shard-7 spec and test are named from reproduced output, not guessed.
- [ ] The fix addresses the root cause (deterministic expectation updated to ruled behavior, or flaky assertion made robust) — no skipped, disabled, quarantined, or deleted test; no raised timeout; no weakened check.
- [ ] The whole shard-7 spec list passes on Chrome against a fresh server boot.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` passes; every touched crate's targeted tests and every touched web test file pass.
- [ ] The pull request names job `e2e (7/8)` and the local shard-7 reproduction used to check it.
- [ ] No file outside the Files to touch table (outside the one failing spec/helper and, if proven, its owning product module) changed.

## Risks

- Changing a spec seed changes what the test covers: keep the seed's documented property (first AI turn observable, Easy game ends by turn 7) and document the new seed's property in the comment, or coverage silently shrinks.
- The `replayHash` folds must keep passing with handicaps included: any spec-13 change must preserve the `handicaps`/`dealt` fields passed to the `replayHash` task, or a real desync hides behind a green test.
- If reproduction shows the AI itself misplays (not just the test's expectation), that is AI-decision work — stop, do not redesign `mulligan.rs`, and re-plan as hard.
- Two runs on one machine must not share the artifacts folder (Cypress empties screenshots at startup): always use `E2E_ARTIFACTS=artifacts/issue-3014`, and stop a started server by port, never by process-name pattern.

## Open questions

- The exact failing test name from the job's log (the linked log needs a person to open; no tool here reaches GitHub). This does not block the builder: the local shard-7 reproduction in step 2 identifies it deterministically. If the local shard passes twice on fresh boots, report that with the run evidence and ask a person to paste the failing test name from the log rather than changing code blindly.
```
